name: Lara Hart
life: “I still remember photographing a faded fishing license under glass.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Lara by a small Monday habit. Lara prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I left a thumbprint when I checked whether the chalk was loose. I'm lending the conservator my steady hand.
appearance: Lara has a dark undercut with a longer wave on top, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. When somebody else has the floor, Lara holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Lara has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Lara can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To repair the loose chalk without disturbing the work.
family: Arthur Colón is Lara’s first cousin once removed. Lara brings a spare shopping bag. Arthur chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Arthur says, “I am the father. I rehearsed an explanation for years and forgot to begin with her name.”
connections: Anthony Ortiz. They decide how to let children make new marks while safeguarding the old ones. Also in the story is Daniel Morris (platform cleaner).

reactions.situation: A contractor wants to scrub the chalk under the quay
reactions.response: Lara takes a photograph and asks whose permission is needed before the chalk is touched.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Lara accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.
